POSITIVE_CTRL_SYNTHETIC_SPA.description: Synthetic deterministic SPA with 8 states, 4 actions, known action->next-state mapping

NULL_CTRL_NORMALIZED_URL.description: Normalized URL PMI (fragment-stripped). Expected exactly 0.0 bits because normalization collapses all URLs to 1 state.
NULL_CTRL_NORMALIZED_URL.expected: Normalized PMI = 0.0 bits on all 5 variants
NULL_CTRL_NORMALIZED_URL.observed: Normalized PMI = 0.000058 bits on 4 variants, 0.000087 on vue. Unique_states = 1 on all 5. Not exactly 0.0 due to Laplace smoothing (alpha=1.0) with 3 unique actions and 1 state.

BASELINE_ACTION_FREQUENCY.description: Action-type marginal distribution across non-leakage transitions
BASELINE_ACTION_FREQUENCY.note: Action frequencies differ from spec predictions due to TodoMVC-specific interaction patterns (form_submit dominates because new-todo input is the primary interaction). PMI conditions all use action_primitive categorical, so frequency differences are captured in the state-conditional computation.

DATA_SUFFICIENCY.observed: 5/5 variants: vanillajs=93, react=93, vue=85, angular=93, svelte=93

observations: Raw URL PMI is significantly positive on ALL 5 TodoMVC hash-SPA variants (0.188-0.209 bits, Bonferroni p=0.001, effect sizes d=6.5-9.0). This is the first demonstration that URL-level PMI detects predictive dynamical structure on real browser-collected SPA transitions when URL fragments are preserved.

Normalized URL PMI is effectively zero (0.000058 bits) with unique_states=1 on all variants, confirming that fragment-stripping normalization destroys all state information encoded in URL fragments. The raw-vs-normalized difference (0.188-0.209 bits) directly quantifies the information loss from standard normalization.

Normalized PMI is not exactly 0.0 due to Laplace smoothing (alpha=1.0): with 3 unique actions but 1 unique state, the smoothed conditional probabilities introduce a tiny non-zero residual. This is a known estimator artifact, not evidence of state information in normalized URLs.

TodoMVC hash-SPAs have only 3-4 unique raw URLs per variant (#/, #/active, #/completed, sometimes trailing slash). The preregistered threshold of >=5 unique raw URLs is an inherent limitation of this testbed, not a failure of URL-level PMI.
Permutation null mean is 0.044 bits (non-zero due to Laplace smoothing inflating sparse counts), but observed PMI is 4-5x the null, yielding very large effect sizes.
All 5 variants have zero singleton state-action pairs, indicating sufficient data density for the PMI estimator (no degenerate sparse cells).

URL entropy (raw) ranges from 1.40-1.96 bits across variants, reflecting 3-4 distinct states. Vue and angular have 3 raw URLs (lower entropy) while vanillajs, react, svelte have 4 (higher entropy including trailing slash variant).
validity_notes: The frozen decision rule Check 2 requires normalized PMI = 0.0 exactly on all 5 variants. This fails because Laplace smoothing (alpha=1.0) introduces a non-zero residual (~0.000058 bits) even with 1 unique state. The 3 unique actions create smoothed conditional probabilities slightly different from 1.0. This is a known estimator artifact, not a measurement failure. The normalized PMI is effectively zero (unique_states=1, url_entropy=0.0 bits).

The frozen decision rule Check 5 requires >= 5 unique raw URLs per variant. TodoMVC hash-SPAs have only 3-4 unique raw URLs (#/, #/active, #/completed, sometimes trailing slash). This is an inherent limitation of the TodoMVC testbed, which was designed as a minimal SPA demonstration, not a rich state-space. The claim is falsified in this specific setting.

Data reuse from parent EXP-PHYSICS-35209110569: no new browser collection was performed. The parent raw transition files are referenced as fixtures. SHA-256 hashes for fixture files were not independently verified in this run (parent integrity assumed).

Cross-trajectory permutation test shuffles action labels within sessions. With mostly deterministic transitions (same (url, action) -> same next_url), the permutation null is well-behaved and the observed PMI is clearly distinguishable.
The positive control (synthetic deterministic SPA with 8 states) validates the PMI pipeline: PMI=1.578 bits, p=0.001. This confirms the estimator detects known structure before testing real data.
unresolved: The frozen Check 2 (normalized PMI = 0.0 exactly) fails due to Laplace smoothing artifact. A future experiment could use alpha=0 (no smoothing) or a threshold-based check (|PMI| < 0.001) to accommodate this known estimator behavior.

The frozen Check 5 (>= 5 unique raw URLs) fails because TodoMVC has only 3-4 unique raw URLs. To satisfy this condition, a richer SPA testbed with more URL states is needed (e.g., a production SPA with multiple routes, filters, pagination).

Raw URL PMI is positive but the magnitude (0.188-0.209 bits) is modest relative to the maximum possible PMI for 3-4 states. The practical utility of this level of predictive structure for SPIDER's exploration task is unclear.

Whether the raw URL PMI signal persists on production SPAs with history-based routing (non-hash) is untested. The TodoMVC testbed uses hash routing which may have different dynamics than production SPAs.
Whether richer state representations (DOM, accessibility tree, visual layout) provide additional PMI beyond URL-only on these TodoMVC SPAs is untested in this experiment.
